name.en-US: A Spiritual Canticle of the Soul and the Bridegroom Christ

description.es-ES: Declaración de las canciones de amor entre el alma y el Esposo Cristo, escrita a petición de la M. Ana de Jesús; segunda redacción, de cuarenta canciones (manuscrito de Jaén). Recorre las vías purgativa, iluminativa y unitiva hasta el matrimonio espiritual. Texto crítico del P. Silverio de Santa Teresa, con sus notas.
description.en-US: St. John of the Cross's commentary on his love-song between the soul and Christ the Bridegroom, written for Mother Anne of Jesus; the second redaction, in forty stanzas (the Jaén manuscript), tracing the purgative, illuminative and unitive ways to the spiritual marriage. Spanish critical text of P. Silverio de Santa Teresa with his notes; English translation by David Lewis, revised by Benedict Zimmerman, from the old printed text of this redaction.
description.pt-BR: Comentário de São João da Cruz ao seu cântico de amor entre a alma e Cristo Esposo, escrito a pedido da Madre Ana de Jesus; segunda redação, em quarenta canções, que percorre as vias purgativa, iluminativa e unitiva até o matrimônio espiritual.

en-US.translator: David Lewis, revised by Benedict Zimmerman

sources.edition: Obras de San Juan de la Cruz, Doctor de la Iglesia, ed. P. Silverio de Santa Teresa, C.D., t. III (Biblioteca Mística Carmelitana), Burgos: El Monte Carmelo, 1930, pp. 181–428 (second redaction). Princeton Theological Seminary scan.
sources.description: Spanish critical text with Silverio's notes (manuscript variants, scripture references) kept as footnotes. OCR of the scan; page furniture removed; footnotes matched to their references page by page; OCR errors corrected by consulting P. Eulogio Pacho's modern text (Editorial Monte Carmelo, via Documenta Catholica Omnia), which was used only to find errors and never copied. Chapter summaries are taken from Silverio's own table of contents.
sources.tierEvidence: San Juan de la Cruz died in 1591. Silverio's edition was published in 1930 (before 1931: public domain in the US) and P. Silverio de Santa Teresa died in 1954, so his text and notes are public domain under life+70 since 1 January 2025. Caveat: Spain applies life+80 to authors who died before 1987, so in Spain alone his notes stay protected until 2035.

sources.edition: A Spiritual Canticle of the Soul and the Bridegroom Christ, translated by David Lewis, with corrections and an introduction by Benedict Zimmerman, O.C.D., 2nd ed., London: Thomas Baker, 1919. University of Toronto scan.
sources.description: English translation with its scripture references as footnotes. Lewis translates the old printed text of the second (40-stanza) redaction, so his paragraphs do not always match Silverio's Jaén text line for line; the stanza divisions match. Zimmerman's introduction and the indexes are not included.
sources.tierEvidence: Published 1919 (before 1931: public domain in the US); the translator David Lewis died in 1895 and the reviser Benedict Zimmerman in 1937, both more than 70 years ago.
